exponent_audit.claim: KTZ dense-core pruning retains Ω(ε) edge mass and minimum degree Θ(εp).
exponent_audit.justification: Revision 1 Lemma 3.1 uses k0=floor(εp/100) and retains incidence measure at least ε/4. Under the nonvacuous cubic hypothesis, the floor changes only constants.

exponent_audit.claim: The sparse selector contributes exactly one inverse power of ε.
exponent_audit.justification: Lemma 3.2 independently samples lines and gives |R|≤6400p/ε while covering Ω(εp) points on every retained line. Chernoff, the union bound, and Chebyshev impose no further ε-power.
The coefficient dimension is Ω(D^3/d), while |R| graph identities impose O(|R|D) equations. Thus D^2=Ω(d|R|), and KTZ's chosen D together with |R|=O(p/ε) gives the displayed upper scale.
exponent_audit.reference: Numbered note 0043, 0260; KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.2 and 4.1–4.2

exponent_audit.claim: The controlling identity/lifting gate is ε^3=Ω(d/p).
exponent_audit.justification: Combining D=O(sqrt(dp/ε)) with the requirement D=O(εp) gives dp/ε=O(ε^2p^2), equivalently ε^3=Ω(d/p).
exponent_audit.reference: Numbered note 0043, 0261; KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 4.3, 5.2, and 6.1

exponent_audit.claim: The ordinary-resultant deletion gives only the weaker square-root condition.
exponent_audit.justification: Its normalized loss is O(D^2/p^2)=O(d/(εp)); making this O(ε) requires ε^2=Ω(d/p). Since 0<d/p<1, (d/p)^(1/2)<(d/p)^(1/3), so this gate is less restrictive than the cubic gate.

exponent_audit.claim: The weighted-resultant exceptional-line loss is O(1/(εp)).
exponent_audit.justification: The bound D^2/d divided by the p(p+1) line normalization is O(D^2/(dp^2)); substituting D^2=O(dp/ε) gives O(1/(εp)).

exponent_audit.claim: The whole-polar term can saturate the cubic balance.
exponent_audit.justification: Theorem C gives loss ε=(D−d)/(p+1)=τ(D−d)/p. With e=D−d=ceil((dp^2)^(1/3)), this is Θ((d/p)^(1/3)) and D=Θ(εp)=Θ(sqrt(dp/ε)).

exponent_audit.claim: The factor-component decoder loses only an absolute factor.
exponent_audit.justification: A cleaned component of minimum degree k yields one polynomial with agreement k/(4p). When k=Θ(εp), this is Θ(ε); the mixing side condition is only ε=Ω(p^−1/2).

It does not claim an improved exponent. Because d/p<1, an improvement would require an exponent strictly larger than 1/3. The verified construction instead occurs exactly at exponent 1/3, and the unconditional benchmark remains unchanged.

line_audit.claim: Theorem A's factor setup and separability claim are sound.
line_audit.justification: Weighted-degree additivity gives sum δ_i=δ. Primitivity rules out base-only factors, and dr_i≤δ_i≤δ

line_audit.claim: The weighted Sylvester degree formula is correct.
line_audit.justification: Every resultant monomial has U/V multidegrees s and r and total Z-coefficient index rs, yielding deg Res_Z(U,V)≤su+rv−drs. The determinant argument remains valid when a specialized leading coefficient vanishes.

line_audit.claim: Exceptional assigned graph lines are bounded by Ξ_i.
line_audit.justification: The nonzero resultant specializes to zero on each common graph, so the corresponding distinct affine-linear base equation divides it. Summed divisorial orders cannot exceed its total degree.

line_audit.claim: Nonexceptional polar intersections are bounded with full multiplicity.
line_audit.justification: The pulled-back polar is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most γ_i, so the sum of orders of its F_p-roots is at most γ_i. Accepted ramified incidences are a subset because acceptance identifies f(x) with P_L(x).

line_audit.claim: The exact and coarse normalized cleanup bounds are correct.
line_audit.justification: Exceptional lines contribute at most p incidences and other lines at most γ_i. Differentiation gives γ_i≤δ_i−d, while Ξ_i≤(2r_i−1)δ_i−dr_i^2=δ_i^2/d−δ_i−(δ_i−dr_i)^2/d. Summing factor degrees yields the coarse expression.

line_audit.claim: Corollary B constructs and propagates one global polynomial.
line_audit.justification: KTZ Lemma 6.1 applies with relation C_i and D=δ_i because more than δ_i incident factor-lines share a simple root. One-variable Newton uniqueness propagates Q through the connected component. The submitted mixing inequalities correctly imply point density at least k/(4p).

line_audit.claim: Theorem C's construction is primitive, squarefree, and has the stated agreement.
line_audit.justification: For e=D−d, B=Z(Z−H) has weighted degree max(2d,d+e)=D, coefficient content one, and two coprime linear Z-factors. Each of p^2 nonvertical lines contributes exactly e accepted incidences, giving ε=e/(p+1).

line_audit.claim: The sharpness roots and concurrency count are exact.
line_audit.justification: On each supported graph B_Z=−H(u+vt), whose e roots are simple. There are ep singular lifted points, each incident to p accepted nonvertical graphs, hence ep^2 ramified incidences. Assignment to C=Z has C_Z=1.

line_audit.claim: The cubic-scale ceiling calculation is correct for every stated parameter.
line_audit.justification: For x=(dp^2)^(1/3) and p≥8d, 4d≤x≤p/2, x≤e≤2x, and D=d+e<p. The displayed absolute bounds on ε and the two Θ-relations follow symbolically.
